clue.text: Lug deacon around French province

indicators.note: around here means the letters of the two words are scattered about into a new order

explanation.surface: A churchman is hauled around a region of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a word of travel, but it tells you to rearrange the letters of LUG DEACON.
explanation.definitionFit: Languedoc is a historic region in the south of France, formerly one of its provinces.

clue.text: Short American volume, risque, showing ability to write

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter of the volume goes

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of the measure litre
racy means risque or slightly indecent

explanation.surface: A naughty little American book proves someone can write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' docks LITER, the American spelling, to LITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the skill of reading and writing.

clue.text: Important person having to arrest old boy

parts.note: to nab someone is to arrest them
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A grandee has to detain a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A nabob is a wealthy or influential figure, originally a returning colonial grandee.

clue.text: Incurable's gone off in radically changed state

indicators.note: off means gone bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: the 's here counts as a letter S in the fodder

explanation.surface: An incurable patient has gone into a markedly altered condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' follows 'gone' as the anagram signal on INCURABLE'S GONE, with the S of the 's included.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so altered that nobody can identify it any more.

clue.text: Great work from type in charge

parts.note: a class is a type or kind

explanation.surface: A masterpiece comes from a particular sort of person in command.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a work of art or literature of lasting excellence.

clue.text: Hard to be taken in by hill god

indicators.note: being taken in by something means going inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough climb up a hill to reach a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a craggy hilltop in the south-west of England; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse deity of thunder.

clue.text: Bob possibly appearing in musical show put on by class

indicators.note: put on by means placed on top of, so the show sits above the class in this down entry

parts.note: Hair is a famous rock musical of the 1960s
style means class or elegance

explanation.surface: A performer called Bob appears in a stylish musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name; it is a short haircut, an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a short haircut, one type of coiffure.

clue.text: Look road — rage erupts at the start

indicators.note: at the start means the jumbled letters go in near the beginning, after the first letter
erupts means bursts out wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Watch out: road rage breaks out at the off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupts' turns RAGE into EGAR, which goes after the R of RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard is to look at or observe.

clue.text: Miss? Miss chortles so uninhibitedly

indicators.note: uninhibitedly means wildly and without restraint, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A young lady laughs loudly and without restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Miss' is the definition; the second is part of the anagram with CHORTLES SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils traditionally address a female teacher as Miss.

clue.text: Potato, maybe, in pot presented to Queen

parts.note: a tub is a pot or container
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A potato in a cooking pot is served up to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks the potato as one example of the class defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a swollen underground stem of the kind botanists call by this name, an example of the class.

clue.text: Looking for indication of burning round church

indicators.note: round means one piece surrounds the other, here the burning word placed around the church

parts.note: searing is a sign that something is being burnt or scorched

explanation.surface: A smell of scorching near a church prompts a hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hunting or seeking something is to be engaged in this kind of search.

clue.text: Patriarch's wife's drunk beer — a very small volume consumed?

indicators.note: consumed means taken in, so the small measure goes inside the other letters
drunk suggests the word beer is in a muddled state, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: CC, a cubic centimetre, is a tiny volume of liquid

explanation.surface: A biblical matriarch has knocked back a tiny drop of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles BEER into REBE; with A after it, 'consumed' puts CC inside, between REBE and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebecca was the wife of Isaac, one of the biblical patriarchs.

clue.text: Liverpool person is, in short, an exploiter when entertaining company

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the pieces hold the company within them

parts.note: is shortened becomes the S of the contraction 's
a user is someone who exploits other people

explanation.surface: A Liverpudlian is accused of being a freeloader at a business function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' cuts IS to the S of 's.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scouser is the informal British name for a native of Liverpool, after a local stew called scouse.

clue.text: Alley cat and corgi in scraps? Definitely

indicators.note: in scraps means torn to pieces, so the animal letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stray cat and a corgi are certainly fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in scraps' sounds like animals fighting; it signals an anagram of ALLEY CAT and CORGI, with 'and' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something categorically is to say it absolutely and without doubt.

clue.text: Limitations to theory about car journal's repetition of ideas

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer letters go around the other pieces
limitations are boundaries, so the first and last letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: auto is a car
a log is a journal or record

explanation.surface: Constraints on a theory about a motoring magazine's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Limitations to' gives TY, the first and last letters of theory, and 'about' puts them round AUTO and LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the same thing twice in different words is a needless redundancy of ideas.

clue.text: Organic compound Helen yet has to blend

indicators.note: to blend means to mix, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist named Helen still has to mix something.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethylene is a hydrocarbon gas, a simple chemical of carbon and hydrogen.

clue.text: Tie tunnelling up? That's 2 stupid

indicators.note: up here means in disorder, as when things are torn up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tunnelling under a tie seems a foolish idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the anagram signal. 'That's 2' reads as 'that's too', a cheeky link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking intelligence is dim-witted, slow or foolish.

clue.text: Port possibly built before railway

indicators.note: before means the jumbled word goes first, ahead of the railway piece
possibly means the letters may take another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harbour that may have been constructed before the line came.
explanation.walkthrough: TILBURY is a port on the Thames in Essex.
explanation.definitionFit: Tilbury is a major port on the Thames estuary in Essex.

clue.text: Nether garments possibly suitable for hill climbing?

parts.note: nether means lower or low down
gear means clothes or garments

explanation.surface: Underwear that might be good for hiking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nether garments' suggests underwear; read separately, the words give LOW and GEAR. The definition describes what the answer does.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottom ratio in a car or bike suits steep climbs, giving more power at low speed.

clue.text: More inclined to spit?

definitions.meaning: skew means slanting, and the comparative form is more slanted
a spit is a rod pushed through meat for roasting

explanation.surface: Is someone more disposed to expectorate?
explanation.definitionFit: A word meaning both more slanted and a long pin for cooking food on.

clue.text: learner becoming a clever Dick?

clue.text: Italian tenor shows cunning, coming across amusingly

indicators.note: coming across means spanning, so the cunning word stretches around the other pieces

parts.note: wily means cunning or sly
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: An Italian singer reveals sly humour on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for 'shows cunning' as a verb phrase; it gives WILY, which spans IT and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking amusingly means doing so with wit and cleverness.

clue.text: One artist to question one Middle Easterner

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A painter is going to quiz someone from the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iraqi is a native of Iraq, in the Middle East.

clue.text: Crawling type starts to wield oar on river, conveying elderly about

indicators.note: starts to means the first letters of the next two words are taken
conveying means carrying, so the river holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England, a regular crossword river

indicators.note: about means the word for elderly is turned around

parts.note: old means elderly

explanation.surface: Someone rowing a boat on a river carries an old person across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns OLD into DLO, which the OUSE, an English river, carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodlouse is a small creeping crustacean found under logs and stones.

clue.text: Dodge publicity in course of previous day

indicators.note: in the course of means during, so the advert sits inside the day

parts.note: eve is the day before an event
an ad, advertisement, is a piece of publicity

explanation.surface: Avoid the press in the run-up to the big day.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge something is to avoid or escape it.

clue.text: Reportedly bring up fish

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word is entered by how it sounds

parts.note: to raise children is to bring them up

explanation.surface: Fish are said to be reared.
explanation.walkthrough: RAISE and RAYS sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are flat cartilaginous sea creatures, such as skates and mantas.

clue.text: Settle here in the north of England?

definitions.text: Settle here in the north of England?

parts.words: Settle here in the north of England?
parts.note: read as an invitation to make a home in the north, but Settle is a market town, and the clue asks which county it lies in

explanation.surface: An invitation to come and live in northern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' looks like a verb but is the name of a market town in the Dales.
explanation.definitionFit: The town of Settle lies in the northern English county, in its North Yorkshire part.
